assessment: The deck carries no sideboard, so all ten are pool scouts. The frame's stated weakness is structural: one Aggravated Assault carries every contained infinite, and the construction corpus is blunt about the fix — a linear deck 'needs redundancy that shrugs off three answers' and should 'sequence so one removal spell can't break the chain' (strategy:critical-mass). Seven of the ten are extra-combat or Treasure engines that give the verified 003/006 Assault architecture a second card name; the other three buy consistency where the role budget is shortest: draw (-6) and early ramp. No pick moves the computed floor off 4.

ten.why: ★ The second Aggravated Assault the deck does not have — an extra-combat effect on a Dragon body, so the eminence discount, Sarkhan's Triumph, and all five spells-only Dragon sources (Haven, Klauth, Maelstrom, Rivaz, Unclaimed Territory) reach its cast; the {5}{R}{R} activation is an ability payment those sources still cannot make, and Treasures fund it exactly as verified stack 006 funds Assault.
ten.unlocks: One removal spell on Aggravated Assault no longer turns off every infinite at once; Old Gnawbone + Charger replays the 006 table-kill under a different card name.

ten.why: ★ Redundancy for the funding half of the verified engine: 'create that many Treasure tokens' on combat damage turns any equipped Dragon into an Old Gnawbone, and it pairs directly with the Assault already sleeved — the most popular line any candidate opens (popularity 34,407) — for three mana.
ten.unlocks: The 006 Treasure-funded loop stops requiring one specific 7-drop; a 3-mana equipment plus any large flier reproduces it.

ten.why: ★ Pays Assault with the one mana type nothing in the deck restricts — untapped lands: on combat damage you untap all lands, covering {3}{R}{R} for the next activation; and in the pilot's white-less pods, protection from black and from green blanks most of the removal that will aim at the engine's carrier.
ten.unlocks: Assault activations stop competing with the deck's spell mana; every connected hit refunds the combat and strips a card from the defender.

ten.why: ★ A second Old Gnawbone for the verified 006 architecture: a d20 of Treasures per connection (mean 10.5, minimum 1 — hence 'near-infinite'; a low roll can undershoot Assault's five mana) on a Dragon body that eminence discounts, Sarkhan's Triumph tutors, and the restricted Dragon mana casts.
ten.unlocks: Doubles the in-99 count of Treasure engines that fund Assault, and its d20 stacks with Ancient Gold Dragon's in the same combat.

ten.why: ★ Untaps all lands on attack — before blockers, not on damage — so it funds Assault even when the attacker is chumped by the token walls the pilot's pods are full of, and umbra armor eats the first removal spell aimed at the creature carrying the engine.
ten.unlocks: An extra-combat loop that never requires connecting — the one funding route no Treasure-based line can claim.

ten.why: ★ A turn-3 dork whose tap makes X unrestricted any-colour mana equal to your greatest power — any 5-power Dragon means Selvala alone pays Assault, and Assault untaps her for the next activation; her draw trigger fires on the deck's own biggest-body Dragons against the role budget's draw -6.
ten.unlocks: The curve-peak turn-3 play that later becomes both combo fuel and a draw engine; the draw trigger is symmetric, but this deck usually owns the biggest body.

ten.why: ★ The only pick whose infinite does not route through Aggravated Assault at all — it pairs with the Scourge of the Throne already sleeved (each copy's dethrone grants another combat; the scenario must verify the attack-the-most-life condition holds each iteration) — and off-combo it stamps a nonlegendary Miirym, Terror of the Peaks, or Old Gnawbone copy every combat.
ten.unlocks: A second, fully independent extra-combat axis, plus a copy engine every verified ETB/damage-trigger stack (001, 002) scales with.

ten.why: ★ Converts damage the Dragons already deal into postcombat red mana that legally pays Assault — five damage covers {3}{R}{R} on its own, and a Drakuseth attack banks ten; ranked below the Dragon-bodied engines because no typal support reaches a Minotaur.
ten.unlocks: Every combat becomes ramp: postcombat main phases cast eminence-discounted Dragons even on turns Assault never fires.

ten.why: ★ Obsolescence-traced (similarity 0.9983, Lower CMC): fetches any Forest card untapped — including the deck's Forest-typed duals — two turns earlier than Skyshroud Claim, as functional copies three and four of the Nature's Lore/Farseek effect the goldfish shows the deck leaning on (71.6% ramp by t6).
ten.unlocks: A ramp spell at the curve's modal turn instead of turn 4, tightening the consistency number the whole wave-deployment plan sits on.

ten.why: ★ The role budget's biggest hole is draw (-6) and this is the pool's largest Dragon-shaped patch: a d20 of cards on connection with no maximum hand size — and verified stack 005 establishes Sneak Attack cheats any 99 Dragon in for {R}, which is exactly how an 8-drop draw engine should arrive; the pilot asked for it by name (pilot_feedback.md).
ten.unlocks: One connection refuels the hand the wrath-math deployment plan spends; eminence, Korlessa, and the Dragon-restricted mana all discount or pay the honest cast.

gaps: Every combo line above is unverified. Highest-value stack scenarios to buy, in order: The Reaver Cleaver + Aggravated Assault Treasure accounting (mirrors verified 006), Old Gnawbone + Hellkite Charger, and Helm of the Host + Scourge of the Throne — the copy's dethrone condition (must each extra combat attack the player with the most life?) decides whether that loop is real.

Ad Nauseam is the pool's only Game Changer candidate (line: Ad Nauseam + Teferi's Protection, infinite card draw, unverified). Excluded on fit, not on floor: the deck's heavy 5-7 shelf makes the life cost brutal, and the pilot's approved bracket 4 means the floor was never the objection.

Pilot feedback names Hellkite Tyrant and Faeburrow Elder; neither appears in any evidence channel. Honest reads: Tyrant's theft line is live in Treasure-token pods (Treasures are artifacts), but at {4}{R}{R} it competes with Hellkite Charger and Ancient Copper Dragon, which end games through the verified Assault architecture instead of borrowing mana from it. Faeburrow Elder fights the deck's shape twice — ramp is already over budget (13/10) and its {W} pip is the deck's thinnest colour (10 land sources). Overriding the data here is a pilot call.
The synergy channel produced only noise for this deck (format-wide 'Ramp + Cost Reduction' shortlists off Savage Ventmaw/Klauth) — no pick carries a synergy_partners_in_deck claim.

Role shorts in lands (-2), sweeper (-2), recursion (-2), and wincon (-3) have no evidenced pool candidate worth a slot: the lands figure is the builder's 36-land prior against the deck's 34 lands, a two-card gap, and the one evidenced wincon (Revel in Riches, line with Old Gnawbone) waits for an upkeep check the verified combat kills don't need.
